requirement: HTTP-message is a request-line CRLF, zero or more field lines CRLF, an empty line, and optional body
notes: Smoke case exercises a complete ordinary request; framing-specific body variants are catalogued separately.

requirement: A response uses a status-line, CRLF-delimited field lines, an empty line, and an optional body
notes: The body-presence cross-reference is RFC 9112 section 6; this row covers the message envelope.

requirement: A sender emits the request start-line and fields with CRLF boundaries
notes: Independent Http1Wire parsing validates emitted boundaries; malformed scripted responses are never production-encoded.

requirement: A sender emits a response status-line and CRLF-delimited fields
notes: The status-only case directly observes the raw first line; the field case parses the complete response.

requirement: Clients expect response start-lines and servers expect request start-lines
notes: No cross-role start-line stimuli yet; general recipient recovery is allowed by RFC 9110 section 2.4, so blanket rejection is not inferred.

requirement: HTTP message syntax has similarities to Internet Message Format and MIME
notes: MIME containers and Appendix B comparisons are outside plaintext HTTP message exchange coverage.

requirement: Parse messages as octets in an encoding that is a superset of US-ASCII
notes: The binary field stimulus includes 80 FF C3 28, an invalid UTF-8 sequence, followed by an independently checked field boundary.

requirement: Octet parsing must not allow malformed multibyte sequences containing LF to change element boundaries
notes: Current binary cases prove opaque byte preservation; invalid multibyte sequences crossing an LF delimiter need additional dedicated stimuli.

requirement: Recipients may recognize single LF and ignore a preceding CR as a line terminator
notes: Acceptance and rejection are both permitted; no standalone pass is awarded merely for either outcome. Missing variants should compare meaning and boundaries if accepted.

requirement: Do not generate bare CR within protocol elements other than content
notes: Valid sender cases contain no bare CR. Adversarial application header values may be rejected before connection establishment, which the current scripted-client lifecycle cannot observe as a completed exchange.

requirement: A bare CR in a protocol element must make it invalid or be replaced by SP before processing
notes: Server outcomes permit empty EOF or an error response with no application observation; accepted values must contain the replacement SP. Target and script errors are isolated. Optional rejection heads permit informational prefixes; complete-response closure permits recognized resets while retaining extra bytes.

requirement: Apply the bare-CR invalidation or replacement rule outside field values too
notes: Request-line and status-line robustness alternatives interact with CR separators; those separate element variants are not yet exercised.

requirement: A user agent must not preface its request with an extra CRLF
notes: The independent peer expects a nonempty request-line as the first line.

requirement: A user agent must not follow a request with an extra CRLF outside its message body
notes: The current request reader stops at the framed boundary; proving no extra output needs a subsequent-exchange barrier, not a sleep or successful first parse.

requirement: Count any desired terminating CRLF in the request body length
notes: Body-framing work owns binary body cases; this syntax fragment does not claim the specific final-CRLF sender variant.

requirement: Ignore at least one empty CRLF line before a request-line
notes: This is a recommendation, not a mandatory-recipient-rejection rule.

requirement: A sender must not emit whitespace between the start-line and first field
notes: Legal sender stimuli are independently parsed; unsafe application-supplied header injection remains separately unobserved.

requirement: Reject or consume every whitespace-preceded line between start-line and the first field without processing it
notes: Two successive SP/HTAB-prefixed lines must both disappear if processing succeeds; the following legal field and body remain intact.

requirement: For message grammar failures outside robustness exceptions, respond with 400 and close the connection
notes: The four negative cases are explicitly SHOULD cases and require real EOF after a complete 400 response.

requirement: HTTP-version uses the case-sensitive HTTP-name followed by slash DIGIT dot DIGIT
notes: Lowercase HTTP-name and two-digit minor examples exercise the section 2.2 recommendation; emitted valid syntax is checked independently.

requirement: HTTP-version grammar permits one digit in each major and minor position
notes: The frozen target contract does not expose a configurable message version; cross-version recipient behavior is not inferred from a syntax-only mismatch.

requirement: When the recipient version is unknown or 1.0, construct 1.1 messages whose newer features can be ignored
notes: Feature-specific framing restrictions are separate; the fixture does not model remembered remote versions or user-agent-specific compatibility policy.

requirement: Intermediaries send their own conformant HTTP-version when forwarding messages
notes: Proxy forwarding is outside the baseline.

requirement: An origin may send 1.0 to a known or suspected broken 1.1 client
notes: Known-broken client attributes and configured compatibility policy are not represented by the frozen scenario contract.

requirement: Do not downgrade a 1.1 response unless specific client attributes trigger it
notes: The frozen target contract does not expose configured compatibility policy, so a syntactically valid HTTP/1.0 downgrade does not fail the status-line grammar test.

requirement: Generate method SP request-target SP HTTP-version with single SP separators
notes: Http1Wire validates exactly three space-separated request-line components.

requirement: Recipients may use whitespace-delimited boundaries including repeated SP, HTAB, VT, FF, or bare CR, ignoring outer whitespace
notes: No mandatory rejection is invented. Each accepted variant would need to prove the same method and target; that matrix is not implemented.

requirement: A method longer than any implemented method should receive 501
notes: Implemented method-length limits are not exposed; ordinary extension-method syntax cases do not prove this boundary.

requirement: A request-target longer than the server wishes to parse must receive 414
notes: No configurable target limit exists in the frozen fixture; an arbitrary large stimulus cannot identify the exact advertised capacity.

requirement: Support request-line lengths of at least 8000 octets
notes: An 8000-octet target yields an 8013-octet request-line, also satisfying the stronger RFC 9110 URI-length recommendation. Failures remain recommendations.

requirement: The method production is token
notes: Valid punctuation covers every nonalphanumeric tchar; the malformed-method recommendation is checked separately.

requirement: Request methods are case-sensitive
notes: A server may return 501 for an extension method; successful application dispatch must retain the lowercase token.

requirement: Method definitions and registry considerations are in RFC 9110 section 9
notes: General method semantics are excluded; CONNECT and HEAD framing dependencies are retained separately. Inventory category: cross-reference.

requirement: The request-target alternatives are origin-form, absolute-form, authority-form, and asterisk-form
notes: CONNECT is exercised with an application 501 response so no tunnel is required.

requirement: Whitespace is not allowed in the request-target
notes: The invalid request uses a literal SP; the legal counterpart encodes it as %20.

requirement: Respond to an invalid request-line with 400 or a 301 redirect carrying a properly encoded target
notes: Both specified alternatives are admitted; the redirect must encode the embedded space.

requirement: Do not silently autocorrect an invalid request-line and apply it to the target resource
notes: The case requires 400 or 301 and no application observation.

requirement: Send a Host field in every HTTP/1.1 request
notes: The no-user-header request must emit exactly one Host naming the loopback IP and an explicit numeric port.

requirement: Host must equal target URI authority after removing userinfo and its at-sign delimiter
notes: The client fixture substitutes its listener authority and does not expose the bound port to the script; arbitrary authority, exact port equality, and userinfo exclusion cannot all be observed.

requirement: If the target URI authority is missing or undefined, send an empty Host value
notes: Both adapters bind client requests to the fixture listener authority; an absent target authority cannot be represented faithfully.

requirement: Respond 400 to any HTTP/1.1 request lacking Host
notes: The phase-1 case covers origin-form; absolute-form without Host remains a missing concrete variant.

requirement: Respond 400 when more than one Host field line appears even when values agree
notes: Duplicates remain ordered raw fields on the wire.

requirement: Respond 400 when more than one Host field line appears with distinct values
Host occurrence counting is case-insensitive
notes: Host and hOsT are separate physical lines for the same field name.

requirement: Respond 400 to a Host port containing nondigit characters
notes: Legal explicit numeric and empty ports have positive counterparts.

requirement: Respond 400 to Host containing a userinfo subcomponent
notes: Host grammar is uri-host with optional port, not the full URI authority production.

requirement: Respond 400 to a comma-list Host value
notes: This is one physical field line with an invalid value, not two field lines.

requirement: Respond 400 to a Host value containing a path
Respond 400 to embedded whitespace in a Host value
notes: Boundary OWS is separately legal and trimmed.

requirement: Respond 400 to an unclosed bracketed IPv6 Host literal
notes: A complete bracketed literal with a port has a positive counterpart.

requirement: For direct origin requests other than CONNECT or server-wide OPTIONS, send only path and query
notes: The path and query include percent-encoded SP; no absolute URI authority may be serialized.

requirement: Send slash when the target URI path is empty
notes: RequestData.path is empty and the raw request-target must be /.

requirement: Origin-form begins with absolute-path and optionally includes question-mark query
The optional query component may be present and empty
notes: The trailing question mark must remain in the application URI rendering.

requirement: Origin-form must not have an empty path, relative path, or fragment
notes: These grammar variants are not yet exercised; RFC 9110 section 2.4 recovery prevents inferring a universal MUST reject rule.

requirement: Use absolute-form for ordinary requests sent to a proxy
notes: The baseline has direct origin clients and servers only.

requirement: Service an absolute-form proxy request locally or forward according to RFC 9110 section 7.6
notes: Proxy forwarding and caching are excluded. Inventory category: cross-reference.

requirement: Send Host even in absolute-form requests to a proxy
notes: Direct client adapters do not expose proxy mode; the origin-server Host requirement remains in scope.

requirement: Ignore received Host and regenerate it from the absolute request-target while forwarding
notes: Proxy forwarding is excluded.

requirement: For absolute-form requests use the request-target host information instead of received Host
notes: The conflicting-Host case proves syntax acceptance only. RequestData exposes original target and fields, not the effective routing authority used internally.

requirement: An origin server must accept absolute-form requests
notes: Acceptance is asserted independently of effective-authority reconstruction, which remains a gap.

requirement: Absolute-form URIs without an authority can arrive with an empty Host value
notes: Non-http schemes and an empty Host interact with routing configuration unavailable in the frozen adapter.

requirement: CONNECT authority-form is uri-host colon port
notes: Only request parsing is covered; a 501 application response avoids exercising a tunnel or proxy.

requirement: A CONNECT client sends only tunnel host and port, adding the default port when omitted
notes: The fixture rewrites the destination authority; RequestData has no distinct tunnel destination or connection handoff operation.

requirement: Only CONNECT uses the authority-form request-target
notes: No sender-invalid method/target pairing is tested because current public-adapter rejection may occur before the scripted socket is accepted.

requirement: Server-wide OPTIONS uses only asterisk as the target
notes: This brings in the OPTIONS target-form dependency only; OPTIONS application semantics are excluded.

requirement: Only server-wide OPTIONS uses asterisk-form
notes: Invalid application method/target pairing is not observed; no mandatory recipient-rejection rule is invented.

requirement: The last proxy rewrites OPTIONS absolute-form with empty path and no query to asterisk-form
notes: Proxy forwarding is excluded.

requirement: An absolute-form request-target is already the target URI and is parsed into generic components
notes: Raw request acceptance is observed, but the contract has no effective-target-URI observation independent of raw path rendering.

requirement: Absent fixed configuration or a trusted gateway scheme, a plaintext target URI uses http
notes: ServerHandle reports method, raw path, and fields, not reconstructed scheme.

requirement: Secured connections use https unless configuration provides a scheme
notes: TLS is excluded.

requirement: A configured fixed scheme or a trusted gateway-supplied scheme takes precedence
notes: Gateway forwarding and deployment-specific configuration are excluded.

requirement: Use authority-form as authority, otherwise use Host, otherwise an empty authority
notes: Effective authority and configured defaults are not exposed by RequestData.

requirement: Authority-form and asterisk-form give an empty combined path/query; other forms use request-target
notes: The adapter reports the received target, not the separately reconstructed URI components.

requirement: Recombine determined scheme, authority, and path/query into an absolute URI
notes: No API observation of the effective reconstructed URI is available.

requirement: Reject an empty required authority or replace it with a configured default consistent with connection context
notes: The contract does not expose default virtual-host configuration. An empty Host is not classified as unconditionally invalid.

requirement: A server that uniquely identifies a secure authority may use it as a safe default
notes: TLS and virtual-host deployment policy are excluded.

requirement: After reconstruction determine whether the target resource is one the server will serve under RFC 9110 section 7.4
notes: General application routing and resource ownership are excluded. Inventory category: cross-reference.

requirement: Emit HTTP-version SP three-digit status-code SP optional reason-phrase
notes: The raw wire assertion observes the space after 299 and validates allowed reason-phrase octets.

requirement: The reason phrase may be absent while its preceding SP remains
Emit the separating SP even when the reason phrase is absent
notes: Reply takes a numeric status but no reason phrase. Generated 299 checks the separator without requiring either adapter to choose an empty phrase.

requirement: Recipients may use whitespace-delimited boundaries including SP, HTAB, VT, FF, or bare CR and outer whitespace
notes: Permitted tolerance does not imply required acceptance. No meaning-preservation matrix for these alternative separators exists yet.

requirement: The status-code production contains exactly three decimal digits
notes: 200 and 299 are sampled. Recipient handling of malformed or out-of-range codes is not asserted as mandatory rejection.

requirement: Accept a valid unrecognized status code with its integer value and response body framing preserved
notes: 299 exercises acceptance, response body framing and exact integer status reporting only; semantic class interpretation is not observed.

requirement: Interpret unrecognized status codes according to their class, including 1xx, 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, and 5xx
notes: An exposed integer status alone cannot prove higher-level class treatment, including for 299; general status semantics are excluded. Informational sequencing and status-dependent body framing are covered separately where available.

requirement: Reason-phrase permits HTAB, SP, VCHAR, and obs-text
Ignore reason-phrase content as an unreliable channel
notes: A 200 response says Not Found; status and body must still be interpreted from 200.

requirement: Reason-phrase excludes other controls and DEL
notes: No blanket recipient rejection is imposed; bare CR normalization is covered in fields, not reason phrases.

requirement: Core status definitions and registration live in RFC 9110 section 15
notes: General status semantics are excluded except class interpretation and body-framing dependencies. Inventory category: cross-reference.

requirement: A field line is token field-name, colon, OWS, field-value, OWS
notes: Unknown field names are intentionally used to exercise generic syntax without a semantic header codec.

requirement: Parse generic field lines independently of individual field names
notes: The raw extension field is delivered through the neutral observation contract.

requirement: Interpret field-specific content after the generic field section has been processed
notes: The harness observes complete application heads but has no independent HTTP/1 partial-header liveness barrier to prove internal interpretation timing.

requirement: Respond 400 to SP between a field name and colon
notes: Uses the phase-1 smoke case; the ID is not duplicated.

requirement: Respond 400 to HTAB between a field name and colon
notes: The legal counterpart uses HTAB after the colon.

requirement: Remove whitespace before a response field colon before forwarding
notes: Proxy forwarding is excluded; the server-specific 400 requirement is not applied to clients.

requirement: OWS before a field value can be absent
Exclude leading and trailing SP and HTAB when extracting a field line value
notes: Mixed SP/HTAB occurs at both ends.

requirement: An empty field-value is legal
A field containing only boundary OWS extracts as an empty value
A single SP before the field value is preferred for readability
notes: The independent message reader discards boundary OWS. Sender spacing policy needs a separate raw-head assertion.

requirement: Outside message/http, reject obsolete request folds with 400 or replace them with one or more SP before processing
notes: The test permits both normative alternatives and forbids exposing the unsanitized field to the application.

requirement: A user agent replaces each obsolete response fold with one or more SP before interpretation
notes: SP, HTAB, and two successive folds are explicit independent cases.

requirement: Do not generate obsolete line folding in ordinary HTTP messages
notes: Short legal field values sample serialization without folding. Automatic folding at longer lengths and unsafe caller values remain untested.

requirement: The obs-fold production permits OWS before CRLF followed by required whitespace
notes: Current fold stimuli use zero OWS before CRLF. Multiple pre-CRLF SP/HTAB and repeated server folds remain missing concrete variants.

requirement: The no-fold generation rule has an exception for message/http packaging
notes: The baseline exercises transport HTTP messages, not message/http MIME containers.

requirement: For an obsolete response fold either substitute 502 or normalize it before forwarding
notes: Proxy and gateway forwarding are excluded. Original scoped role: proxy,gateway.

requirement: A sender must not generate elements that violate their defined grammar
notes: Representative valid public-API inputs only; this is not exhaustive proof of invalid application-input handling.

requirement: A sender must not generate malformed elements even when application input is invalid
notes: The frozen client scenario waits for a socket before it can complete; rejection during request construction can occur without any accepted socket. A separate pre-connect rejection observation is needed.

requirement: Do not generate alternatives reserved for a role the participant does not hold
notes: No intermediary or cache target is instantiated by this baseline. Original scoped role: proxy,gateway,cache.

requirement: Parse elements defensively without relying on ABNF compliance or reasonable sizes
notes: The finite syntax cases sample invalid elements but do not bound parser memory, CPU, or all overlong element classes.

requirement: Accept element lengths at least as long as elements the implementation itself generates
notes: No paired configurable sender/recipient maximum is exposed; the 8000-octet recommendation is a separate concrete case.

requirement: Unless a specific rule says otherwise recipients may recover usable elements from invalid constructs
notes: Covered cases constrain explicit RFC-required alternatives only. Generic grammar failures are not automatically mapped to MUST reject. Response-head byte and informational-count ceilings are typed incomplete observations; they cannot establish malformed output or successful rejection.

requirement: Apply defined semantics unless experience or configuration establishes a broken sender
notes: Known-implementation workaround configuration and semantic policy are unavailable; ordinary syntax is tested without such triggers.

requirement: Some requests may be retried after connection failure under section 9.2.2
notes: General retry policy is outside syntax scope; a timeout or script failure cannot count as rejection. Inventory category: cross-reference.

requirement: HTTP version numbers comprise a major decimal digit and a minor decimal digit
notes: Wire syntax is checked through RFC 9112. Claims about sender conformance are not inferable from the version token alone.

requirement: Absolute-path is one or more slash-segment components and may begin with a double slash
notes: This grammar differs from RFC 3986 path-absolute, which forbids a double-slash prefix.

requirement: Imported query grammar permits slash and question mark, and may be empty
Imported URI segment/query syntax carries reserved data via percent encoding
notes: Includes encoded SP, slash, hash, and question-mark octets without normalizing the wire stimulus.

requirement: Protocol elements select URI-reference, absolute-URI, partial-URI, or their imported components
notes: The suite does not exhaust imported RFC 3986 grammar productions; relative references, fragments, IPvFuture, percent-escape failures, and authority edge cases beyond Host remain missing variants.

requirement: Support at least 8000-octet URIs in protocol elements
notes: The request URI is exactly 8000 ASCII octets, independent of the larger request-line length.

requirement: An http URI contains scheme, authority, path-abempty, and optional query
notes: Both nonempty path/query and empty-path legal absolute-form are accepted.

requirement: Reject an http URI with an empty host identifier as invalid
notes: An error response or genuinely empty connection EOF is allowed; application acceptance is forbidden.

requirement: Do not generate an http URI with an empty host
notes: The fixture replaces request authority with its bound listener address before the client operation.

requirement: The http scheme uses port 80 when the port is empty or absent
notes: All target connections use an explicitly bound ephemeral loopback port. The legal Host empty-port syntax is covered without claiming routing-to-80 behavior.

requirement: Field names use the token production
notes: Every permitted punctuation tchar appears in the legal field name; the delimiter rejection is a SHOULD recommendation.

requirement: Field names are case-insensitive
notes: Host interpretation and duplicate detection exercise semantics beyond merely retaining the original spelling.

requirement: Client field interpretation is case-insensitive
notes: The syntax cases preserve original field occurrences but do not vary the case of a semantically parsed response field; framing variants may cover this independently.

requirement: Forward unrecognized fields unless Connection or configured transformation permits removal
notes: Proxy forwarding is excluded.

requirement: An unrecognized field should not prevent a recipient from processing a message
notes: Fields remain visible to the adapter application; their extension semantics are not interpreted or required.

requirement: For a field appearing once its field value is its one extracted line value
For repeated names concatenate field line values in received order with commas
notes: Connection is a registered list field. No test requires the implementation to retain multiple physical lines in its application representation.

requirement: Recipients may combine same-name lines in order with commas and optional whitespace
notes: The oracle accepts separate occurrences or their legal combined representation by comparing ordered list tokens.

requirement: A forwarding proxy must not reorder same-name field values
notes: Proxy forwarding is excluded.

requirement: A sender may emit repeated field lines when their definition permits list recombination
notes: The Connection field uses the registered list syntax; an arbitrary unknown extension field is not assumed to be list-based.

requirement: A sender must not emit duplicate singleton fields or append an incompatible repeated field line
notes: Unsafe raw application fields may fail before the wire connection is observed; the suite currently tests recipient Host duplicates, not sender singleton validation.

requirement: Set-Cookie is a well-known exception that cannot be safely comma-combined
notes: Cookie grammar and semantics are outside the frozen RFC set; this exception is explicitly retained in the inventory rather than generalized to other fields. Inventory category: exception.

requirement: Order among fields of different names is not significant
notes: Current stimuli contain several orders but no dedicated permutation case proves equivalence independently of same-name ordering.

requirement: Sending control data such as Host and Date first is good practice
notes: The neutral decoder preserves order but no preferred-order sender assertion is implemented.

requirement: Do not apply a request before its entire header section has arrived
notes: A single poll before the final CRLF would be a racy absence test. The contract has no independent HTTP/1 liveness barrier for proving this timing invariant.

requirement: Respond with an appropriate 4xx when field line, value, or section size exceeds accepted limits
notes: Per-target limits are not configurable or observable, so no guessed size is used as a universal rejection threshold.

requirement: A client may discard or truncate oversized fields only when message framing and semantics remain safe
notes: The contract lacks a field-limit setting and a field-specific semantic observation for proving safe omission.

requirement: Field-value permits zero field-content instances
Field-content may contain SP and HTAB between field-vchar octets
notes: Boundary trimming must not erase the interior HTAB/SP sequence of the opaque field value.

requirement: Exclude version-permitted leading and trailing whitespace before evaluating a field value
Treat obs-text octets 80-FF as opaque field content
notes: 80 and FF cover both bounds; C3 28 is deliberately invalid UTF-8. The adapter exposes one character per input octet for these raw field values.

requirement: Reject CR and NUL within field values or replace each with SP before processing
notes: The CR rule is also imported directly by RFC 9112 section 2.2.

requirement: Reject LF within a field value or replace it with SP
notes: A single LF may itself be a permitted line terminator under RFC 9112 section 2.2. A future case must distinguish value interpretation from legal delimiter recognition instead of asserting blanket rejection.

requirement: Other CTLs are invalid but may be retained in a safe application-specific context
notes: The contract does not identify a safe downstream context; neither universal acceptance nor universal rejection would be a valid oracle.

requirement: New field specifications should constrain values to visible ASCII, SP, and HTAB
notes: This suite consumes existing protocol fields and does not register a new field specification.

requirement: Field definitions should disambiguate commas and use compatible token or quoted-string parameter meanings
notes: Design of new field semantics is outside the wire-target scope; imported list and quote syntax dependencies are inventoried separately.

requirement: A sender using list syntax must not generate empty list elements
notes: A generic raw header API can be supplied invalid lists; its pre-connect refusal cannot currently be observed without waiting for an absent peer connection. Valid repeated Connection values are covered.

requirement: Parse and ignore a reasonable number of empty list elements and exclude them from cardinality
notes: This needs a semantically interpreted framing or Connection-list case; raw field preservation does not prove list-parser behavior. No such coverage is claimed by this syntax fragment.

requirement: Token is one or more tchar; punctuation is exactly ! # $ % & apostrophe * + - . ^ _ backtick | ~
notes: All punctuation alternatives appear explicitly; ordinary methods and names also cover letters and digits.

requirement: A token must contain at least one character and exclude whitespace and delimiters
notes: An illegal method delimiter and field delimiter have recommendation cases, but empty method/name and the complete delimiter matrix remain missing.

requirement: OWS consists of zero or more SP or HTAB octets
RWS consists of one or more SP or HTAB octets
notes: The concrete RWS use here is RFC 9112 obsolete folding; field-specific RWS semantics are not generalized from opaque fields.

requirement: Generate preferred OWS or RWS as a single SP and otherwise avoid unnecessary OWS
notes: Sender raw-spacing assertions are not implemented; field extraction intentionally normalizes boundary OWS.

requirement: Known OWS and RWS may be replaced by one SP before interpretation
notes: The grammar determines where whitespace is OWS or RWS; an arbitrary opaque field interior must not be treated as universally normalizable.

requirement: Do not generate bad whitespace where grammar preserves it only for historical reasons
notes: BWS in framing parameters is owned by the framing corpus; generic field-line OWS is not mislabeled BWS.

requirement: Parse and remove BWS before interpreting its protocol element
notes: Chunk-extension and transfer-coding parameter cases belong to the framing inventory; this fragment has no dedicated BWS semantic oracle.

requirement: A quoted-string is DQUOTE followed by qdtext or quoted-pair and a closing DQUOTE
notes: Opaque field delivery cannot prove quoted-string parsing. Framing parameter variants are inventoried by the framing author.

requirement: A recipient processing quoted-string replaces each quoted-pair by its following octet
notes: The frozen response/request observation exposes raw values and does not expose a general parsed parameter value; mere preservation of a backslash is not evidence of processing.

requirement: Use quoted-pair only when needed for quote or backslash in quoted-string, or parentheses/backslash in comments
notes: The scenarios do not generate parsed field parameters or comments; no mandatory rejection of unnecessary escapes is imposed.

requirement: Host is uri-host with an optional colon port
notes: Includes a registered name, numeric port, bracketed IPv6, and the legal empty port production.

requirement: Host conveys target URI host and port under a case-insensitive name
notes: The case proves recognition of hOsT; effective routing authority remains unobservable.

requirement: Generate Host unless authority is supplied as an HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 pseudo-header
notes: HTTP/1.1 has no authority pseudo-header alternative; HTTP/2 coverage is owned by its separate inventory.

requirement: A user agent should send Host as the first field in the request header section
notes: The outgoing Host-presence case preserves raw order but does not assert this preference; caller-provided header ordering needs an explicit policy decision.
